question: Kamet, Namcha Barwa, Gurla Mandhata are the names of:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**mountain peaks in Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kamet** is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India. It stands at an elevation of 7,756 meters.
 
• **Namcha Barwa** is a mountain in Tibet, and it is known as the eastern anchor of the Himalayas. It has an elevation of 7,782 meters.
 
• **Gurla Mandhata** is located in Tibet, near the sacred lake Manasarovar, and has an elevation of 7,694 meters.
 
• These peaks are part of the greater **Himalayan mountain range**, which spans five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan.
 
• The Himalayas are home to some of the world's highest peaks, including **Mount Everest** and **K2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rivers flowing through Himalayas**__

 __
 
• The Himalayas are the source of many major rivers, including the **Ganges, Indus, Brahmaputra, and Yamuna**.
 
• These rivers are crucial for the agriculture, hydropower, and drinking water needs of the region.
 
 
 
• **Tribes living in Himalayas**__
 __
 
• The Himalayas are home to various indigenous tribes such as the **Sherpas, Ladakhis, and Bhutias**.
 
• These tribes have unique cultures and traditions that have been preserved over centuries.
 
 
 
• **Volcanoes in Himalayas**__
 
 
• There are no active volcanoes in the Himalayas.
 
• The region is primarily known for its tectonic activity, which has led to the formation of the mountain range.
